decisions.question: A run-down lead-acid house battery freezes in deep cold and is lost. I graded that a moderate risk, so its setting starts on. Do you agree?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.333.0 (row 640). One battery kit is lost, over about half a day, with a warning when it starts; running the engine, shore power or a warmer place saves it. The setting is 'Run-down house batteries freeze' (Vehicle Systems, Camps). The shared rule: a risk starts on unless it is high or higher.

options.label: High: starts off
options.detail: A player chooses it; by default a lead-acid house battery never freezes

decisions.why: A slow loss of one kit, warned of, with three ways to stop it, is what the rule calls low or moderate

decisions.question: Where should a lead-acid house battery cut the camp loads off?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.333.0 (row 640) at half its charge, my default, on the common practice of drawing lead-acid deep-cycle batteries to about half for a long life (unverified). With no wear modelled (your card), the cut-off is the only thing that makes lead-acid cost more than lithium, which cuts off at a tenth.

options.label: Half, as built
options.detail: 50 Ah usable of 100; the low warning at 60 %

options.label: A third
options.detail: About 67 Ah usable: gentler, nearer what a low-voltage cut-off often allows

options.label: A fifth
options.detail: 80 Ah usable: closer to lithium, so lithium's gain is mostly its weight and the cold

decisions.why: It keeps the two batteries clearly different while wear is not modelled, and matches how such batteries are really used

decisions.question: Parked off the grid with the engine off, should a fuel heater run from the starting battery?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.334.0 (row 648), my choice: it draws 12 A in deep cold from the alternator, the grid or the battery, and goes out before the battery is too low to start the engine, after which the fuel can gel. It only matters with 'Fuel thickens in deep cold' on.

options.label: Yes, down to the start line
options.detail: As built: a few hours of protection parked, then it goes out with a message

options.label: No: engine or grid only
options.detail: As real ones are wired to the ignition; parked off the grid the fuel can gel at once, and the battery is never drawn

decisions.why: It gives a camped vehicle some hours of grace and makes the battery matter, while still never stranding the engine

decisions.question: The fittings audit left four smaller gaps open. Should I close them?
decisions.context: Listed in the audit's record: a crew water tank taken off leaves its water behind on the vehicle; fitting a deep-cycle starting battery tops the battery up a little; kit electrical loads (remote control kit, radar, rescue hoist, jamming pod) draw the same amps on a 24-volt vehicle, so twice the watts; and the Prowler's improved jamming suites do not yet say they need power.

options.label: Close all four
options.detail: One batch: water and charge travel or are lost honestly, kit loads follow the voltage, the text is corrected

options.label: Only the voltage and the text
options.detail: The two a player can notice; the water and the battery top-up give no real gain

options.label: Leave them
options.detail: They stay listed in the record

decisions.why: The 24-volt draw doubles what a kit costs on every heavy truck and aircraft; the other two change nothing a player could exploit
